citations.description: _built_client_kwargs accepts allow_insecure but no test passes allow_insecure=True to assert options['verify'] is still not False; no test simulates a verification failure naming ca_bundle

findings.criterion: TLS certificate verification is never disabled — asserted against the parameter form the library ACTUALLY reads. The test must also assert a verification failure raises an error naming the `ca_bundle` setting rather than silently proceeding. `allow_insecure` is asserted to affect the URL scheme check ONLY — a test confirms it does not relax certificate verification
findings.detail: Two sub-requirements of this AC are not met. (1) There is no test asserting that a TLS verification failure raises an error naming the `ca_bundle` setting. The existing tests (`test_tls_verification_is_never_disabled`, `test_a_ca_bundle_configures_verification_rather_than_disabling_it`) verify that `options['verify']` is never False and that a ca_bundle path is passed correctly, but neither simulates an SSL/cert error and checks that the resulting error message names `ca_bundle`. (2) There is no test that explicitly passes `allow_insecure=True` to `build_client_from_settings` and asserts that `options['verify']` is still not False — i.e., that `allow_insecure` does not relax certificate verification. The `_built_client_kwargs` helper in `test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py` accepts `allow_insecure` as an override but no test exercises that path to assert the cert-verification invariant holds.
